set.name: Two Voices
set.mechanism: Builder and creative in one line: heavy wide capitals say the fact, an italic serif word says the feeling, so the caption system, the italic wordmark and the espresso-and-maple palette all come from the same two-voice sentence.
set.expression_move: The italic serif word inside a line of heavy capitals: the only loud thing, used once per post.
set.differs_by: zerotoui uses one heavy sans in white and Asterisk Create pairs a serif with red-orange on grass green and mustard; this keeps the two-voice caption but sets it on espresso and bone white with one maple orange, so the feed reads as fall rather than studio or field.

logo.concept: The name in the creative voice, ended by the builder's voice: a lowercase italic 'shay' with one heavy square full stop in maple.
logo.defect: Plain italic name had nothing ownable; added the square maple full stop that carries the heavy-caption voice into the mark.

defaults_used.why: Shay asked for whites and browns with a fall feel; the bone ground is the white of that request, kept close to white rather than yellow cream.
Shay asked for a fall palette and pointed at Asterisk Create's red-orange captions; maple is pushed redder and more saturated than clay, and there is no gold accent with it.

rationale.claim: Heavy capitals plus an italic serif word is the caption style Shay pointed at in both reference feeds.
Archivo's width axis gives wide black capitals for captions and a normal-width 400 for reading from one family, so the second face is only the italic.
Bodoni italic at large optical size has the drama of the reference captions; it is kept to display sizes because hairlines thin out when small.
Espresso and maple on bone reads as fall; that association is taste, not evidence.

palette.name: Two Voices
palette.direction: Espresso ink on bone white, with one maple orange for the feeling word.

brand.name: Maple
brand.usage: the italic feeling word in captions; one per screen

set.name: Race Bib
set.mechanism: A race bib pinned at four corners: the mark is the bib with SHAY punched through it, the type is a condensed athletic grotesk like a printed start number, and the palette is bib white, trail brown and Forest City pine.
set.expression_move: The bib shape itself, pinned on everything from the profile picture to the end card.
set.differs_by: None of the reference creators has a mark at all, only captions; this gives Shay an object people can recognise in a 16 px avatar and that belongs to training and building alike (you pin a bib on before you start).

logo.concept: A start bib with four pin holes and the name punched through: you pin it on before you build or race.

rationale.claim: Shay wants the brand to work for a training and health lifestyle as well as building; a race bib belongs to both starts.
Pine green names London, Ontario's Forest City, where Shay studied at Western; the local meaning is a private nod, not a requirement to read the mark.
A condensed grotesk at 800 holds four capitals inside a small bib and stays legible at avatar size.

palette.name: Race Bib
palette.direction: Trail brown on bib white, with Forest City pine for second surfaces.

set.name: Low Light
set.mechanism: The shot after training, when the light drops: a quiet lowercase name in near-white on bark brown, split once along a low horizon, with Okanagan sage kept for the one highlight per screen.
set.expression_move: The horizon cut through the wordmark; everything else stays dark and still.
set.differs_by: The training creators Shay likes are moody and cool grey; this keeps the low-light mood but warms it to bark brown and adds a sage only Shay uses, with no loud captions at all.

logo.concept: A lowercase 'shay' split low along a horizon, like the last light across a dark frame.
logo.defect: Round 3: the sage line through the middle read as a strikethrough (crossed-out name); now a clean horizon cut low in the x-height, no line in the gap. Sage moves to UI highlights.

rationale.claim: The fourth reference feed is dark, low-saturation and cinematic; this set is built dark-first for that content.
One family keeps the voice quiet and the web load small; hierarchy comes from weight only.
A light warm figure on a dark ground is a well-rated pairing direction.
Sage for the Okanagan's late-season hills is taste and a private nod.

palette.name: Low Light
palette.direction: Bark brown night ground, near-white type, one Okanagan sage.

brand.name: Okanagan Sage
brand.usage: the horizon line, links, one highlight per screen
